D.treatment: desktop VE-based simulation with visual and auditory interaction

O.outcome_detail: perceived multisensory immersion, attractiveness, and enjoyment of repeated practice

cells.quote: Almost all participants reported that the D-VSim not only provided visual perception, but also stimulated auditory sensation, which was consistent with previous research [44]. They also perceived that the D-VSim made repeated activity more immersive and attractive, which could not be achieved with previous traditional training.
cells.note: Qualitative interview perceptions; no quantitative effect size or controlled comparison was reported.

D.treatment: desktop VE-based simulation

O.outcome_detail: understanding and following ADL skill-training procedures

cells.quote: The textual description of skill training is lengthy and obscure, particularly when expressed with a cluster of jargon. Fortunately, I can understand the meaning of each paragraph and follow the steps of each activity by using the D-VSim system. It truly saves a great deal of time and effort. [P9]
cells.note: Participants perceived the simulation as improving understanding relative to conventional PowerPoint learning; no objective learning measure was reported.

D.treatment: desktop VE-based simulation

O.outcome_detail: interest, enjoyment, and initiative to learn

cells.quote:

cells.note: The study reports participants' perceptions of increased engagement and initiative, not a controlled comparison of motivation.

D.treatment: desktop VE-based simulation with repeatable practice

O.outcome_detail: willingness to continue studying and repeat activities

cells.quote: It is much fun using the virtual simulation for learning as it changes the original way of thinking that learning is a tedious process. cells.note: This is a participant-reported perception of persistence; the quoted claim is not an experimentally measured duration or completion outcome.

D.treatment: desktop virtual environment-based simulation

O.outcome_detail: perceived reinforcement of foundational knowledge

cells.quote: The virtual simulation should be used as an auxiliary learning tool. To be precise, virtual simulation is better functional as a post-class rather than an in-class learning strategy. [P12]
cells.note: This is a participant perception from a qualitative interview, describing virtual simulation as complementary reinforcement rather than a replacement for PowerPoint learning.

D.treatment: later training attempts

O.outcome_detail: learning-curve stabilization and proficiency

result.effect: Plateau reached after the fifth training attempt; proficiency criterion was 10 or more attempts with scores of 85 or higher consecutively three times

cells.quote: The learning curves revealed significant improvements in the performance of Fellows and Residents after training, with no significant differences in the total time (p=0.675), the economy of the exercise (p=0.649), or the overall score (p=0.802). Particularly during the first 4 training periods, the trainees' performance improvements were most noticeable in terms of total time, performance of the activity, and total score, after the 5th training, the learning curves reached the platform period, and the trainees' performance began to stabilize.
cells.note: This is a repeated-attempt learning-curve analysis among trained participants; the reported p values compare Fellows and Residents, not early versus late attempts.

cells.note: GEARS scores were evaluated by 10 graduate students with non-medical backgrounds who were trained and blinded to the operation videos.
